data.one_liner: A Dart package for parsing text flexibly using multiple regular expression patterns.
data.what_it_does: It parses text into a structured list of text elements based on preset or custom regular expression patterns. It supports features like groups capture, synchronous parsing, and background execution using isolates.
use_when: You need to detect and extract URLs, email addresses, or phone numbers from text.
You want to parse custom markdown or HTML elements using regular expressions.
You need to parse large texts without blocking the main UI thread.
avoid_when: You need a full context-free grammar parser (use petitparser instead).
You are parsing heavy structured documents like arbitrary XML or complex JSON where dedicated parsers are safer.
strengths: Includes useful preset matchers for URLs, emails, and phone numbers.
Supports running parsing tasks in an isolate to prevent UI jank.
Allows custom matchers and exact string matching with escaped regex characters.
weaknesses: Reliance on regular expressions can become hard to maintain for highly complex nested grammars.
Named capture groups lose their names in the resulting groups list.

alternatives.name: petitparser
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose petitparser if you need a robust grammar-based parser rather than regular expression matching.

alternatives.name: xml
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose xml if your specific parsing target is XML instead of generic text patterns.
